The Keyed Verification Anonymous Credentials (KVAC) paper-formalization repo is now public :tada:

https://github.com/Beneficial-AI-Foundation/KeyedVerificationAnonymousCredential-model

We are formalizing Orrù's Revisiting Keyed-Verification Anonymous Credentials (ePrint 2024/1552) in Lean 4 over Mathlib and VCV-io. Signal plans to move its production credential system to the paper's μCMZ scheme, and this project machine-checks the cryptography underneath it.

This repo is the paper route. It models the paper's definitions, schemes, and security games abstractly, independent of any implementation. A companion effort verifies the KVAC implementation crates themselves and goes public separately. The -model suffix marks the split.

Getting involved

CONTRIBUTING.md describes the workflow and docs/PLAN.md the overall design. Comment on a track issue to claim it, or ask in this channel.

If you want to see where things stand, the project board, docs/TRACKS.md, and the formalization-progress table track current progress, and the rendered blueprint shows the formalization chapter by chapter.

We cloned it today and the build was green on the first try (lake exe cache get, then lake build, 3299 jobs on the pinned v4.28.0, macOS). Reading PLAN.md, the import rule around Instances/ stood out: only Examples/ and the security tracks can import concrete bindings, so the implementation-agnostic boundary around Core/ and Framework/ is enforceable straight from the import graph. 
We'll be watching the tracks fill in, and keeping an eye out for the implementation- side companion when it goes public.
